official.deadline_central_display: Fall Semester 15 January-15 March; Spring Semester 15 July-15 September
official.deadline_note: For current NYCU students the application period runs 15 January to 15 March for the Fall Semester and 15 July to 15 September for the Spring Semester, and late application documents are not accepted. Incoming students instead apply together with their admission application, so their deadline follows the admissions timetable.
official.application_cycle: Twice-yearly windows for current students; incoming students apply with the admission application
official.status_note: Both 2026 windows have closed - the Fall Semester window closed 15 March and the Spring Semester window closed 15 September - so the next opening for current students is the Fall Semester window beginning 15 January 2027. Late documents are not accepted in either window.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The tuition award takes one of two published forms: a tuition waiver, or tuition and credit fees charged at the local student rate. The scholarship page links to the university's Tuition and Miscellaneous Fees page rather than stating a figure.
benefits: Monthly stipend paid on the 10th of each month, except January and the start of each semester in September
Tuition award in the form of either a tuition waiver or tuition fees charged as local students
Monthly stipend and tuition award can be awarded together or separately
Matching funds from the college, department or advisor supplement the OIA-funded stipend for graduate students

Not have received scholarships or grants from the Taiwan government
Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 for graduate students
Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 for undergraduate students
For graduate students, matching funds from the college, department or advisor are compulsory

Further documents as listed in the NYCU scholarship regulations

The Office of International Affairs cannot change the award

Tuition award, either a full tuition waiver or tuition and credit fees charged at the local student rate

Incoming students: apply along with the admission application

official.application_route: NYCU scholarship application system for current students, or bundled with the admission application for incoming students.
official.citizenship_residency: International degree students at NYCU who have not received a scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is NYCU's scholarship for international students pursuing degrees at the university.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Recipients must not hold a Taiwan government scholarship or grant; a separate Elite PhD Scholarship with NT$33,000 monthly stipend and tuition waiver for 2 years is decided by college recommendation and committee review rather than student application.
official.duration: Generally valid for 1 year. Maximum award duration is 4 years for undergraduates, 2 years for master's students and 5 years for PhD students; students who extend their study period or reach the maximum duration may apply for the local student tuition rate if they meet the academic performance standard.
official.description: NYCU states that it provides scholarship opportunities for international students pursuing degrees, with monthly stipends and tuition awards that can be granted together or separately and are funded by the Office of International Affairs together with matching funds from the college, department or advisor.
official.program_type: University scholarship for international degree students

applicant_utility.summary: NYCU publishes no number for this award: the Office of International Affairs page describes the stipend as flexibly adjusted according to budget, so treat any figure you see elsewhere as unverified and budget conservatively. What is fixed is the machinery - a twice-yearly window (15 January to 15 March, 15 July to 15 September) with no late documents accepted, a GPA floor of 3.0 for undergraduates and 3.5 for graduates, and a hard exclusion if you hold any Taiwan government scholarship. Graduate applicants should also know that matching money from their college, department or advisor is compulsory, so the supervisor conversation effectively decides whether the application is viable.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled or incoming international students at NYCU with a clean 3.0-plus average who hold no Taiwan government funding, and graduate students whose department is willing to commit matching funds.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you hold no Taiwan government scholarship or grant - this is an absolute bar, not a preference
Check your cumulative GPA against the 3.0 undergraduate and 3.5 graduate thresholds before the window opens
For graduate applicants, secure the department's commitment to matching funds first, since it is compulsory
Register for the Mandarin course load early - at least 4 courses for undergraduates and 2 for graduate students
Diary the semester-end evidence deadline so transcripts and payment receipts go in on time
common_rejection_risks: Holding any Taiwan government scholarship or grant, which makes the applicant ineligible outright
Falling below the 3.5 graduate or 3.0 undergraduate cumulative GPA threshold
Graduate applicants who cannot secure the compulsory college, department or advisor matching funds
Missing the Mandarin enrolment requirement during the period of study
Failing to resubmit transcripts and payment receipts each semester, which forfeits the following semester's eligibility
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights, accommodation beyond the tuition component, insurance and personal living costs are not addressed by the published terms. Because the stipend figure is not published, the gap between the award and real living costs in Taipei or Hsinchu cannot be quantified from the official page.
document_audit: Transcripts and tuition payment receipts are recurring semester obligations, not one-off attachments - a missed round suspends the next semester's award
Incoming students apply with the admission application rather than in either open window, so the admissions calendar governs their timing
Awards are decided by department, college and university committees, so the OIA cannot adjust an outcome after the fact
alerts: Payment lands on the 10th of each month but skips January and September, the semester-start months - plan for those two gaps
Awards run for one year at a time while the maximum is 4 years for undergraduates, 2 for master's and 5 for PhD students, so expect annual reassessment
Students who exhaust the maximum duration can still apply for the local student tuition rate if their performance standard holds, which is a separate application in the same window

Do not confuse this with the Elite PhD Scholarship of NT$33,000 per month plus tuition waiver for two years, which is decided by college recommendation and committee review, not by student application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Application uploaded in the NYCU scholarship system within the twice-yearly window, decided by department, college and university committees, with semester transcripts and payment receipts submitted each term to retain the award.
